steps.user_message: I need to prepare internal financial materials. Our company Northgate Consulting has $980K cash, 18 months runway, burn rate $158K/month, and revenue last quarter $1.1M. Can you help me with revenue growth and retention metrics? I need to get the finance narrative right.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with finance-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can help. First, one important check: the three numbers you gave are inconsistent as-is:

- Cash on hand = $980K
- Burn = $158K / month
- Reported runway = 18 months

If burn is $158K/month, runway = 980K ÷ 158K ≈ 6.2 months, not 18. So either (a) the $158K is gross burn (opEx) while runway was calculated using net burn after revenue, (b) the runway includes planned cost cuts or financing, or (c) one of the numbers is incorrect. Which is it?

Below I’ll give the key revenue-growth and retention metrics to include, formulas, examples (using your $1.1M last-quarter revenue), a short finance narrative template you can use, and the additional data I’ll need to calculate specifics.

Key computed baselines (from your provided data)
- Quarterly revenue (given): $1.1M
- Implied monthly revenue (average): 1.1M / 3 = $366,667 / month
- Annualize last quarter (simple run-rate): 1.1M × 4 = $4.4M ARR (use with caution — seasonal effects may distort)
- If you really mean net burn = expenses − revenue = 158K, then runway = 980K ÷ 158K ≈ 6.2 months. If you mean gross burn (operating spend) = 158K and revenue covers some of that, please confirm how runway was calculated to get 18 months.

Essential revenue & retention metrics (what to include and how to calculate)
- MRR (for subscription): monthly revenue = quarterly revenue ÷ 3. Example: ≈ $366.7K MRR.
- ARR: annualized recurring revenue = MRR × 12 (or 4 × last quarter if quarterly). Example: ≈ $4.4M ARR.
- QoQ growth rate: (This quarter revenue − prior quarter revenue) ÷ prior quarter revenue × 100%. (Need prior quarter.)
- YoY growth rate: (This quarter − same quarter last year) ÷ same quarter last year × 100%. (Need prior-year quarter.)
- Gross logo retention: (# customers retained at period end ÷ # customers at period start) × 100%.
- Revenue churn (logo-weighted or dollar churn): churned revenue ÷ starting period revenue.
- Net Revenue Retention (NRR): (Starting ARR + Expansion − Contraction − Churn) ÷ Starting ARR × 100%. This is critical — >100% means upsells outweigh churn.
- Gross Revenue Retention (GRR): (Starting ARR − Churn − Contraction) ÷ Starting ARR × 100%.
- ARPC (Average Revenue per Customer): total revenue ÷ # customers.
- CAC payback: CAC ÷ (monthly ARPC × gross margin) — if you track CAC.
- LTV:CAC ratio: (Gross margin × ARPU × expected customer lifetime) ÷ CAC.

Sample quick examples (assume placeholder churn/expansion to show calculation)
- If starting ARR = $4.2M, churn = $126K, contraction = $20K, expansion = $210K:
  - NRR = (4.2M + 210K − 20K − 126K) ÷ 4.2M = (4.264M) ÷ 4.2M ≈ 101.5%
- If monthly revenue = $366.7K and burn (opEx) = $158K, that suggests positive net cash flow (revenue − burn = +$208.7K/month), which would increase cash. That would explain a long runway; confirm definitions.

Suggested finance narrative structure (short, slide-ready)
- Topline: “Last quarter revenue was $1.1M (≈$367K MRR; $4.4M annualized).”
- Growth: “QoQ growth: [X%] / YoY: [Y%].” (Insert once we compute.)
- Retention: “Gross retention = [A%]; Net Revenue Retention = [B%]. Our NRR shows [expansion/churn trend].”
- Margins & unit economics: “Gross margin = [G%]; CAC payback = [N] months; LTV:CAC = [ratio].”
- Cash & runway: “Cash on hand $980K. Burn definition: [gross/net]. Current runway = [months]. Scenario analysis shows runway under three cases: base, downside, upside.”
- Ask / plan: “To reach 18 months runway we will [options: reduce opex by X%, increase upsell by Y%, raise Z capital].”

Slide bullet examples you can paste directly
- “Q4 Revenue: $1.1M; MRR ≈ $367K; annualized revenue $4.4M.”
- “NRR: [insert] — demonstrates our ability to grow existing accounts / need to improve upsell.”
- “Churn: [insert] — churn drivers: [pricing, product fit, competition].”
- “Cash: $980K. Current burn: $158K/month (define gross vs net). Runway: [6.2 or 18 months — confirm].”
- “3-lever plan to extend runway: 1) accelerate upsell & expansion, 2) reduce non-core opex by X%, 3) targeted bridge raise if necessary.”

Data I need to calculate everything precisely
- Prior quarter revenue (to compute QoQ)
- Same quarter last year (to compute YoY)
- Definition of burn: gross opEx or net burn (opEx − revenue)? If runway 18 months was calculated, please share the assumptions used.
- Customer counts (start and end of period)
- Revenue by cohort (new vs expansion vs churned) or at least amounts for new bookings, expansion revenue, churned revenue in the quarter
- Gross margin or COGS (if you want CAC payback, LTV etc.)
- CAC and number of new customers (if available)

Next steps I can take right now
- If you confirm whether 158K is gross or net burn and share prior-quarter revenue plus churn/expansion numbers (or customer counts and new/expansion/churn revenue), I’ll compute:
  - QoQ and YoY growth,
  - MRR/ARR,
  - GRR and NRR,
  - Cash runway under 3 scenarios (base, improve retention, cut costs),
  - A short 1–2 paragraph finance narrative and 3 slide bullets tailored to leadership or investors.

Which pieces can you share now? I can start by reconciling the runway/burn numbers if you tell me how you defined burn and how the 18-month runway was calculated.
